name: Opening-range break continuation, opening-range-scaled stop (intraday, fires most days)
notes: LEARN: the opening-range break fires on 72.6% of sessions -- Amendment 1's sourcing preference produced a genuinely intraday candidate on the first try (91.5 projected trades in six months against the 40 required, NOT SLOW). What it also produced is the cleanest cost lesson in the book: gross +$526.33 over 1,525 trades is +$0.35 per trade, and the ASSUMED $6.00 round trip is seventeen times that. A trade that fires most days has to clear roughly 0.10R of cost EVERY day; frequency and edge trade against each other and this one had all frequency and essentially no edge. SECOND: the day's own range is an EX-POST label and its salvage result is close to a tautology -- breakouts work on days that expanded. The knowable PRIOR-day half of the same condition has no signal at all, which is direct evidence that range expansion is not forecastable from the prior day for this trade, and it is why the ex-post split was refused rather than spawned.
